question: Excluding the non-recurring IEEPA tariff refund benefit, what was Costco's Q4 FY2026 diluted EPS, and what was the YoY growth on that basis vs Q4 FY2025?
grading: Adjusted EPS ±$0.01; growth ±0.5pp; must use the per-share benefit as disclosed by Costco and 16-week Q4 columns
answer: Costco Q4 FY2026 diluted EPS excluding the disclosed net tariff-refund benefit was $6.60 ($6.75 - $0.15), up 12.4361% from Q4 FY2025 EPS of $5.87. Both quarters contained 16 weeks. The $0.15 benefit is already net of partial reinvestment in member values. [G15-E1]

output.answer:
**Q4 FY2026 diluted EPS, excluding the IEEPA tariff refund benefit: ~$6.60**

- Reported Q4 FY2026 diluted EPS: **$6.75** (net income $2.998B), which included a one-time benefit of **$0.15/share** from IEEPA tariff refunds (net of partial reinvestment in member value).
- Excluding that item: **$6.75 − $0.15 = $6.60**.
- Q4 FY2025 diluted EPS (as reported): **$5.87**.

**YoY growth on that basis:** (6.60 − 5.87) / 5.87 ≈ **+12.4%**

This matches the characterization in coverage of the print — the headline ~15% EPS gain "becomes 12.4% without the one-time refund."

Note: this uses prior-year reported EPS of $5.87 (the comparison the company/market used). All figures are for the 16-week fourth quarter ended August 30, 2026.

Sources:
- https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/costco-shares-slip-11-jump-183514381.html (EPS $6.75 vs $5.87; $0.15 IEEPA benefit)
- https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/costcos-best-numbers-came-asterisk-132700449.html (15% gain → 12.4% ex-refund)
- https://au.finance.yahoo.com/news/costco-tops-q4-estimates-revenue-210613585.html (Q4 net sales/EPS detail)
